near_miss_chains.description: A resource tagged with a high-sensitivity classification (confidential, restricted, PII, PHI, PCI) is stored in or accessed from an unprotected storage resource — one that is publicly accessible, lacks encryption, or has both. The classification tag declares the data as sensitive; the storage posture contradicts that declaration. Individually the classification and storage controls may pass their own checks; the compound finding is that the two together create a gap.

PHI data reachable from public internet with no encryption or audit trail — total safety envelope failure. Any two of these co-failing creates a compound risk because the data is both exposed and either unprotected or unmonitored.

A non-production resource (staging, dev, test, qa, sandbox, demo) is dormant AND publicly reachable. The compound is the canonical NHI-offboarding failure mode: forgotten ephemeral infrastructure retained on the internet, beyond active maintenance, accumulating configuration drift. Stave's per-service public-access controls fire on each individual exposure dimension (S3 bucket policy, EC2 SG ingress, API Gateway resource policy, ALB topology); the staleness control fires on the lifecycle-plus-environment-tag combination. Either alone is a finding; both on the same asset is the shadow-infrastructure crisis the writeups in channels/devto/ describe.
